author: Jason Stys
summary: Use accessible table sorting, paging, stable missing-value ordering and focus handling. Final TGZ acceptance now installs the actual public package into an external React/Vite consumer and exercises shipped behavior, CSS and accessibility in Chromium.
rationale: Proves that the packaged public exports work in a genuine separate consumer instead of passing because export names appear in JavaScript text.
limitations: An installable component library and catalog, without automatic npm publication or a native desktop installer.
Synthetic component/browser checks and zero automated axe findings do not certify accessibility or replace manual assistive-technology testing.
Archive integrity and locked peers identify tested bytes, not independently authenticated publishers or OS code signatures.

visualReview.method: Every rendered page individually viewed at readable original resolution

scope: Reviewed documentation editions of the cited source. Checksums identify bytes, not authorship. Historical measurements retain their own dates; integration CI must be checked separately.
